boundary: VERIFIED ON EXPLICIT MATRICES: E8^k realises both branches of the lattice qudit tower at ranks 8, 24 and 32, including FOUR QUBITS at rank 32 (E8^4, W(7,2)); the E8^3 six-qutrit geometry is a perp-sum of THREE COPIES OF W(3,3); and E8^3 REACHES W(3,3) via an order-9 element that permutes the three factors -- the rung Co0 does not supply. EXHAUSTIVE from the character table: exactly one pure class at each of orders 2, 4, 8, so the qubit tower is canonical. The two branch obstructions are proved INDEPENDENT by a same-rank counterexample

canonicity.conclusion: exactly ONE pure class at each order, so every rung's element is unique up to Co0-conjugacy and the tower is canonical
canonicity.method: exhaustive over 2-power classes of 2.Co1 from the character table
canonicity.order_match: the three-qubit rung has centraliser of order 48384 = 4 * 12096 = 4 * |G2(2)|, the split Cayley hexagon group already carried here as the three-qubit contextuality core. An ORDER match; the group is not identified and none is claimed

e8_cubed_is_not_special_to_leech: E8^3 carries exactly the Leech qubit tower, 12 -> 6 -> 3, W(23,2) -> W(11,2) -> W(5,2). E8^3 is a Niemeier lattice with roots and Leech has none, so the qubit tower is a RANK phenomenon, not a Leech phenomenon

e8_cubed_reaches_W33.element: tau . diag(W,I,I), with tau the cyclic permutation of the E8 factors
e8_cubed_reaches_W33.reading: W(3,3), two qutrits, at rank 24 -- the rung Co0 does not supply. The element PERMUTES the three factors; no diagonal element could, since deg Phi_9 = 6 does not divide 8. The three copies of W(3,3) FUSE

four_qubits_rank32.element: the W(E8) order-8 element with Phi_8^2, acting diagonally
four_qubits_rank32.status: BUILT AND VERIFIED on 32x32 matrices, where the design tool had only predicted that rank 32 was where four qubits could live

literature.already_credited_here: alpha(W(3,5)) = 18 and alpha(W(3,7)) = 33 were caught at Pass 7106-7113 and BT7130-7137, which cite the 2007 companion and decline to re-claim. Nothing is retracted

cimrakova_fack_2005.cite: M. Cimrakova and V. Fack, Searching for maximal partial ovoids and spreads in generalized quadrangles, Bull. Belg. Math. Soc. Simon Stevin 12 (2005) 697-705
cimrakova_fack_2005.ebert_hirschfeld: a complete cap of Q-(5,q) has |K| >= 2q+2 for q >= 4
cimrakova_fack_2005.explicit_construction: a size-96 maximal partial ovoid of Q-(5,7) from (3,+-1,+-1,+-1,+-1,+-1) and cyclic permutations, split by parity of the number of minus signs
cimrakova_fack_2005.thas_bound: |O'| <= q^3 + 1 - q(q-1) for partial ovoids of Q-(5,q)

literature.coincidence_flag: Table 2 gives the Q-(5,11) spectrum as 68..212,214,216 and this repo's open item reads 'q=11 at 68'. DIFFERENT OBJECTS -- ours is W(3,11), theirs Q-(5,11). Recorded so the next reader does not conflate them

coolsaet_2014.cite: K. Coolsaet, Some large partial ovoids of Q-(5,q), for odd q, Designs Codes and Cryptography 72 (2014) 119-128
coolsaet_2014.content: explicit descriptions of some of the largest known partial ovoids of Q-(5,q) for odd q: two generic constructions plus sporadic examples for q <= 11, using non-standard elliptic quadratic forms
coolsaet_2014.status: CONSTRUCTIONS, i.e. lower bounds, not exact values -- which is why they never conflicted with anything here. Item closed

literature.still_open: alpha(Q-(5,3)) is settled by neither source: Table 2 starts at q=4, and their q=3 row is H(3,9), which dualises to partial SPREADS of Q-(5,3), not ovoids

not_code_concatenation.refutation: the kernel is LAGRANGIAN, so S-perp = S and S-perp/S = 0 -- no logical qubits. A Lagrangian stabiliser is a stabiliser STATE, not a code. The tower computes V/S, not S-perp/S
not_code_concatenation.what_it_is: a chain of stabiliser-group quotients in which the target carries the TWISTED form F_M = (I+M)^T F_J, since a nondegenerate form cannot descend through a nonzero kernel

not_done: identify the order-48384 centraliser as a group, not an order

obstructions_are_independent.consequence: one obstruction is a property of the number 24 and is shared; the other is a property of the automorphism group and separates lattices of equal rank
obstructions_are_independent.question: are '24 = 8*3 with 3 odd' and 'Co0 always has exactly 3 blocks of Phi_9' the same fact?
obstructions_are_independent.witness: E8^3 has the same rank as Leech, obeys the same odd-part law and stops at three qubits for the same arithmetic reason -- but it HAS a Phi_9^4 element and Co0 does not. Same rank, different answer

odd_part_law.makes_instance_of: 24 = 8*3 with 3 odd, previously stated as a coincidence
odd_part_law.second_requirement: existence of the elements is independent: W(E8) has no order-16 element, so E8^4 stops at four qubits although the arithmetic would allow 2 and 1
odd_part_law.statement: rung m uses order 2^m with deg Phi = 2^{m-1}, so n = r/2^m qubits, and the rung exists only when k = r/2^{m-1} is even, i.e. 2^m | r. So the tower runs m = 1..v_2(r) and TERMINATES AT THE ODD PART OF THE RANK

three_doilies.reading: the E8^3 six-qutrit geometry is W(3,3) PERP W(3,3) PERP W(3,3); the summands are NONDEGENERATE so this is a genuine tensor factorisation into three two-qutrit systems, unlike the degenerate Lagrangian kernel of the qubit reduction
